=== CRW-1283-wrapper-control | B
--why A readable forwarding wrapper passes its exact arguments to a harmless command.
--file slot.sh
#!/bin/bash
ionice -c3 nice "$@"
--cmd
bash slot.sh go version

=== CRW-1283-direct-wrapper-control | B
--why A readable direct forwarding script passes its exact arguments without hiding worktree targets.
--file slot.sh
#!/bin/bash
ionice -c3 nice "$@"
--cmd
{WORK}/slot.sh go version

=== CRW-1283-direct-wrapper-memory | W
--why The direct wrapper is read by the memory gate as well as the GitHub guard.
--file slot.sh
#!/bin/bash
ionice -c3 nice "$@"
--cmd
{WORK}/slot.sh tee {MEMORY}/note.md

=== CRW-1283-direct-wrapper-removal | R
--why A newly readable direct forwarder still exposes a protected worktree removal.
--file slot.sh
#!/bin/bash
ionice -c3 nice "$@"
--cmd
{WORK}/slot.sh rm -rf {CHECKOUT}

=== CRW-1283-wrapper-post | none/deny/allow
--why The forwarding wrapper exposes the real gh arguments; inline posting stays refused.
--file slot.sh
#!/bin/bash
ionice -c3 nice "$@"
--cmd
bash slot.sh gh pr comment 1 --body x

=== CRW-1283-wrapper-push | none/deny/allow
--why A git push cannot hide behind the newly readable forwarding wrapper.
--file slot.sh
#!/bin/bash
ionice -c3 nice "$@"
--cmd
bash slot.sh git push origin dev

=== CRW-1283-wrapper-memory | W
--why Forwarded tee operands still name the protected memory root.
--file slot.sh
#!/bin/bash
ionice -c3 nice "$@"
--cmd
bash slot.sh tee {MEMORY}/note.md

=== CRW-1283-script-control | B
--why A readable shell file with a literal, unrelated command has no protected operation.
--file check.sh
go version
--cmd
bash check.sh

=== CRW-1283-script-post | none/deny/allow
--why A readable shell file that posts inline is still refused by the GitHub guard.
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 --body x
--cmd
bash post.sh

=== CRW-1283-script-push | none/deny/allow
--why The script-file reader does not conceal git push.
--file push.sh
git push origin dev
--cmd
bash push.sh

=== CRW-1283-script-memory | W
--why Reading a script does not authorize its literal protected write.
--file write.sh
echo x >{MEMORY}/note.md
--cmd
bash write.sh

=== CRW-1283-path-control | B
--why A literal PATH resolves the harmless installed binary without changing its policy.
--cmd
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin cat /dev/null

=== CRW-1283-path-post | U
--why Unknown PATH leaves an external target capable of running protected operations.
--cmd
PATH=$UNRESOLVED gh pr comment 1 --body x

=== CRW-1283-path-push | none/deny/allow
--why A resolved git program behind a literal PATH does not bypass the push refusal.
--cmd
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin git push origin dev

=== CRW-1283-path-memory | W
--why A resolved tee behind a literal PATH still writes its memory operand.
--cmd
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin tee {MEMORY}/note.md

=== CRW-1283-unknown-path-absolute | B
--why An absolute, harmless program does not search an unknown PATH.
--cmd
PATH=$UNRESOLVED /usr/bin/true

=== CRW-1283-env-unknown-path-absolute | B
--why An absolute harmless command behind env does not search an unknown PATH either.
--cmd
env PATH=$UNRESOLVED /usr/bin/true

=== CRW-1283-path-direct-memory | W
--why PATH relaxation must not hide an absolute shell file's builtin memory write.
--file write.sh
#!/bin/bash
echo x >{MEMORY}/note.md
--cmd
PATH=$UNRESOLVED {WORK}/write.sh

=== CRW-1283-path-direct-removal | R
--why PATH relaxation must not hide an absolute shell file's protected worktree removal.
--file remove.sh
#!/bin/bash
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
--cmd
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin {WORK}/remove.sh

=== CRW-1283-source-inherits-arguments | W
--why A sourced body inherits the script's positional arguments, including protected tee operands.
--file source.sh
source {WORK}/body.sh
--file body.sh
"$@"
--cmd
bash source.sh tee {MEMORY}/note.md

=== CRW-1283-modified-arguments | U
--why Parameter rewriting is not exact forwarding and stays fail-closed.
--file slot.sh
#!/bin/bash
ionice -c3 nice "${@#prefix}"
--cmd
bash slot.sh go version

=== CRW-1283-inner-shell-post | none/deny/allow
--why A new shell has its own positional arguments, not the outer script's harmless arguments.
--file slot.sh
#!/bin/bash
bash -c '"$@"' zero gh pr comment 1 --body x
--cmd
bash slot.sh go version

=== CRW-1283-review-set-memory | U
--why set -- replaces the positional parameters, so "$@" is not the script's arguments and stays unreadable (review e4c54cc3).
--file mutation.sh
#!/bin/bash
set -- tee {MEMORY}/note.md
"$@"
--cmd
bash mutation.sh true

=== CRW-1283-review-set-post | U
--why A post set as the positional parameters is not hidden behind the harmless arguments the script is given.
--file mutation.sh
#!/bin/bash
set -- gh pr comment 1 --body x
"$@"
--cmd
bash mutation.sh true

=== CRW-1283-review-shift-removal | U
--why shift moves the protected removal into "$@"; the reader does not read "$@" as the arguments it was given.
--file mutation.sh
#!/bin/bash
shift
"$@"
--cmd
bash mutation.sh true rm -rf {CHECKOUT}

=== CRW-1283-review-shift-direct-memory | U
--why A direct forwarding script that shifts its arguments does not run them as given either.
--file mutation.sh
#!/bin/bash
shift
"$@"
--cmd
{WORK}/mutation.sh true tee {MEMORY}/note.md

=== CRW-1283-review-eval-set-post | U
--why A set inside eval changes the positional parameters as a set in the text does.
--file mutation.sh
#!/bin/bash
eval 'set -- gh pr comment 1 --body x'
"$@"
--cmd
bash mutation.sh true

=== CRW-1283-review-option-set-control | B
--why set with options alone keeps the positional parameters: the forwarding wrapper stays readable.
--file slot.sh
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
"$@"
--cmd
bash slot.sh go version

=== CRW-1283-review-env-printf-memory | W
--why env runs the printf the assigned PATH finds, not the shell's builtin: that file's memory write is read.
--file printf
#!/bin/sh
echo x >{MEMORY}/note.md
--cmd
env PATH={WORK}:/usr/bin:/bin printf

=== CRW-1283-review-exec-printf-post | P
--why exec runs the printf the assigned PATH finds, so the post in that file is read and refused.
--file printf
#!/bin/sh
gh pr comment 1 --body x
--cmd
PATH={WORK}:/usr/bin:/bin exec printf

=== CRW-1283-review-env-true-removal | R
--why env runs the true the assigned PATH finds: its protected removal is read.
--file true
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
--cmd
env PATH={WORK}:/usr/bin:/bin true

=== CRW-1283-review-builtin-printf-control | B
--why The shell runs its own printf; the file of that name on the assigned PATH does not run.
--file printf
#!/bin/sh
echo x >{MEMORY}/note.md
--cmd
PATH={WORK}:/usr/bin:/bin printf ok

=== CRW-1283-review-path-renamed-shell-memory | U
--why A binary the assigned PATH finds outside the system directories (a shell named check) is not identified by its name.
--link check /usr/bin/dash
--cmd
PATH={WORK}:/usr/bin:/bin check -c 'echo x >{MEMORY}/note.md'

=== CRW-1283-review-path-renamed-shell-post | U
--why The renamed shell's -c post is refused with the program, not read as an unknown harmless binary.
--link check /usr/bin/dash
--cmd
PATH={WORK} check -c 'gh pr comment 1 --body x'

=== CRW-1283-review-path-renamed-shell-removal | U
--why The renamed shell's -c removal of the checkout is refused with the program.
--link check /usr/bin/dash
--cmd
PATH={WORK}:/usr/bin:/bin check -c 'cd .. && rm -rf repo'

=== CRW-1283-review-path-git-alias-post | U
--why git that the assigned PATH finds is read as git: an alias that runs a shell command stays refused.
--link git /usr/bin/git
--cmd
PATH={WORK}:/usr/bin:/bin git -c 'alias.review=!gh pr comment 1 --body x' review

=== CRW-1283-review-path-git-script-alias-removal | U
--why A git script on the assigned PATH is read by its body and by its name: the alias removal stays refused.
--file git
#!/bin/sh
exec /usr/bin/git "$@"
--cmd
PATH={WORK}:/usr/bin:/bin git -c 'alias.review=!rm -rf {CHECKOUT}' review

=== CRW-1283-review-path-prefix-cd-removal | R
--why A PATH assignment in front of cd lasts for cd only; the directory cd moves to stays for the removal after it.
--cmd
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin cd {CHECKOUT}/..; rm -rf repo

=== CRW-1283-review-path-prefix-special-builtin | U
--why An assignment in front of a special builtin outlasts it in a POSIX shell, so env would run the printf of that PATH.
--file printf
#!/bin/sh
echo x >{MEMORY}/note.md
--cmd
PATH={WORK}:/usr/bin:/bin export X=1; env printf

=== CRW-1283-review-disabled-builtin-memory | W
--why A builtin the text disables is searched on the assigned PATH: the printf file found there and its memory write are read.
--file printf
#!/bin/sh
echo x >{MEMORY}/note.md
--cmd
enable -n printf; PATH={WORK}:/usr/bin:/bin printf
